Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:28: The reason is as I have explained: since the days are a garment for the soul, and a day is a portion of a small stature within that garment, it is accounted as though he blemished the entire year. Therefore great care is needed not to blemish any of his days, and if, Heaven forfend, he has caused a blemish, he should repent on that very day - in the manner of (Avot 2:10), "repent one day before your death," which our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 153a) to mean that all his days should be found in repentance. My teacher, peace be upon him, explained that the intent is that his days should be illuminated from the secret of supernal repentance - just as, in the Ten Days of Repentance, repentance repairs all the days of the year because they all return to it, so too, through returning each and every day by itself, they are illuminated from repentance, and they are all found repaired before the Day of Judgment of Rosh Hashanah and the Ten Days of Repentance arrives.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:29: And so Rashbi says (Vayechi 220a), in these words: "but the worthy, pious ones examine their hearts every day, as though on that very day they were to depart from the world, and perform complete repentance before their Master, so that they will not need anything else in the World to Come" - to this point. And what he means by "will not need anything else" refers to what is explained, that the [supernal] image withdraws from a person, and it depends on whether he repents or not - and likewise regarding the matter of the records handed to the messengers, explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:30: Let us return to our subject: it is said that he is judged in Gehinnom day for day, doubled. From this we derive that since he is punished doubly, it is fitting that, upon his repentance, he should perform commandments and Torah every day doubly - increasing in the commandment of tefillin, evening and morning, and everything within his power, and likewise visiting the sick, and increasing in charity, and similarly in all the commandments of loving-kindness - and he should repent, for through repentance he repairs the deficient days; and this is a great virtue of repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:31: Further, concerning the blemish pertaining to the days, the commentators explain that in the twelve hours of the day and night, twelve permutations of "the LORD" revolve, one permutation each hour; and if, Heaven forfend, a person causes a blemish, he blemishes that [divine] Being that revolves in that hour. This is similar to what the pious one said (see Chovot HaLevavot, Gate of the Service of God, chapter 5): do not rebel against your Master while He watches over you.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:32: Further, it is explained that there are 4,096 [parts in an hour, per an esoteric reckoning: "tatr"af"], and corresponding to them is the four-letter Name that revolves through the permutation of its vocalization in the alphabet, 4,096 permutations; and it says that these 4,096 parts of the hour are 4,096 breaths that a person breathes, and for every single breath there is a letter of the four-letter Name that gives that breath its vitality - and this is (Deuteronomy 8:3), "for by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD does man live." And since God, blessed be He, is the One who gives breath and life, it is fitting that all his breaths be for the service of the Creator. To this our Sages, of blessed memory, alluded in Bereshit Rabbah (14:9), on the verse (Psalms 150:6), "let every soul [breath] praise the LORD" - Rabbi Levi, in the name of Rabbi Chanina, said: for every single breath a person breathes, he must praise the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, "let every soul [breath] praise the LORD" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:33: When a person considers this matter, he will fear to sin and will conduct himself with humility and lowliness - for how could he sin and treat lightly the life that God, the King, bestows within him? My teacher, peace be upon him, used to say that for this reason the books of Heichalot (Rabbati 18:4) call God, blessed be He, "the insulted King" - for there is no greater insult than this: that with the very life He bestows within a person, and with the limbs He prepared for him to serve Him, he sins against Him. He likened this to a king who gave his servant money to buy bread to sustain himself, and the servant came and bought, with that money, a stick to strike his master - is there a worse servant than this? And yet God, blessed be He, is insulted and overlooks the offense and is slow to anger - how much more so should one formed from a putrid drop be careful not to transgress His attributes, as we shall elaborate, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10:34: Rashbi, peace be upon him, summarized all these blemishes in these brief words (Naso 122a), in these words: "whoever transgresses the commandments of the Torah, as it were, blemishes above, blemishes below, blemishes himself, blemishes all the worlds - for these separate his days," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:1: There are several further particulars concerning the fear that comes from judgment. One must fear the several witnesses who testify against him every day, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 16a), on "do not trust a friend [ba-re'a]" (Micah 7:5) - Rabbi Yehuda bar Nechemiah, the interpreter for Reish Lakish, expounded: what is meant by "do not trust a friend [ba-re'a]"? Do not trust the evil one [ba-ra]; do not rely on a companion [aluf] - if the evil inclination tells you, sin, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will forgive you, do not believe it, as it is said, "do not trust ba-re'a" - and "ra" [evil] refers only to the evil inclination, as it is said (Genesis 8:21), "for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth"; and "aluf" [companion/master] refers only to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:4), "You are the companion [aluf] of my youth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:2: Perhaps a person will say, who testifies against me? The stones of his house and the beams of his house testify against him, as it is said (Habakkuk 2:11), "for the stone shall cry out from the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it." Rabbi Sheila said: the two ministering angels who accompany a person testify against him, as it is said (Psalms 91:11), "for He shall command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways." Rabbi Chidka says: a person's soul testifies against him, as it is said (Micah 7:5), "guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your bosom" - what is it that lies in a person's bosom? You must say, this is the soul. And the Sages say: a person's limbs testify against him, as it is said (Isaiah 43:12), "and you are My witnesses, says the LORD, and I am God" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:3: And in Ra'aya Meheimna (Shoftim 275a), this passage is explained, in these words: "and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established: who testifies against a person? The beams of his house - and not only that, but the people of his house testify against him. What is meant by 'the beams of his house'? These are the beams of the heart - (Isaiah 38:2), 'and Hezekiah turned his face to the wall' - this teaches that Hezekiah prayed from the walls of his heart. 'The people of his house' - these are his two hundred forty-eight limbs, for the masters of the Mishnah established: a wicked person's sins are engraved on his bones - and therefore it is said, who testifies against a person? The beams of his house. And the bones are built upon the marrow, which is water, and of them it is hinted (Psalms 104:3), 'who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters' - 'mekareh' [lays beams] is a term related to 'korot' [beams]. And why specifically in the bones, more than the flesh, sinews, and skin? Because the bones are white, and black writing is discernible only against white - like the Torah, which is white within and black without; white within is light and darkness [both]. And there is a darkness that is 'techelet' [sky-blue], of which it is said (Psalms 139:12), 'even the darkness is not dark to You' - and techelet is the female counterpart to white."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:4: And not only that, but the body is destined to be resurrected upon the bones, and therefore his merits and sins are engraved on his bones - if he merits, the body will be resurrected upon his bones, and if not, it will not be resurrected, and he will almost have no share in the resurrection of the dead. And not only that, but there are two witnesses against a person: the eye that sees and the ear that hears, and a court that records and judges his sins. And not only that, but the sun and moon are witnesses against a person, as has been established," and so on - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:5: Now, from the introduction to this passage, which says that a wicked person's sins are engraved on his bones and he almost has no share in the resurrection, we may understand (Proverbs 5:11), "and you shall mourn at your end, when your flesh and body are consumed, and you shall say, how I have hated instruction!" The matter is that every ordinary person, even a righteous one, has no suffering except while the garment of flesh is intact - for the worm is as hard for the dead as a needle in living flesh, as it is said (Job 14:22), "but his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn" - as I have explained at the end of chapter twelve of this Gate, that after the flesh decomposes, the righteous one has rest and has "release of the bones," as it is said (Isaiah 58:11), "and He will give strength to your bones [or: release your bones]." But the wicked one, after the judgment of the flesh and the judgment of the grave, still has his sins remaining upon his bones, and then he moans and says, "how I have hated instruction," and so on - and this is "at your end, when your flesh and body are consumed" - meaning at the end, after the flesh is consumed in the grave - "and you shall say," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:6: Further, "your flesh and body" [besarcha u-she'ercha] may mean to teach us that all the pleasures of this world are transient and perishable - the reason being that the flesh is from the husk [kelipah], and therefore decay rules over it, except for the completely righteous, who refine their flesh in this world, over whom the worm has no power at their death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:7: Now, the primary limb that desires physical pleasure is through the covenant [brit], and the covenant is called "flesh" [basar], as it is said (Jeremiah 11:15), "and the holy flesh has passed from you" - and he desires his wife, who is called "she'er" [flesh/kin], as it says (Leviticus 21:2), "except for his flesh [she'ero] who is near to him" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, explained that "she'ero" refers specifically to his wife. When a person considers that all the limbs that desire pleasure will be nullified and perish, he will come to refrain from pursuing the vanities of the world, which are perishable and transient - and this is the intent of "your flesh [besarcha] and your body [she'ercha]." And he uses the second person "your flesh" to teach that the flesh a person builds up for himself by following the vanities of the world decays and perishes; but one who sanctifies his flesh and derives pleasure only from a meal connected with a commandment, as I explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15, that flesh is not ruled over by the husk [kelipah].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:8: And in this manner we may understand the verse (Job 14:22), "but his flesh upon him shall have pain" - meaning that the flesh he built up is what will have pain upon it, "and his soul within him shall mourn" - for how it drew the husk upon itself. But flesh built up through meals connected with a commandment has no pain upon it, and his soul does not mourn, Heaven forfend - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:9: The passage of Rabbi Sheila, who said that the angels who accompany a person are the ones who testify against him, appears to follow the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Vayeshev 191a), in these words: "and nevertheless, a person must examine his sins every single day, for when a person rises from his bed, two witnesses stand before him and go with him all day. When a person wishes to rise, those witnesses say to him: 'let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids look straight before you' (Proverbs 4:25). He rises and prepares his feet to walk; those witnesses say to him: 'make level the path of your feet,' and so on. Therefore, as a person goes about each day, he must guard himself from his sins every single day; when night comes, he must examine and review all that he did that whole day, so that he may repent from them, and he should always reflect on them so that he may return before his Master, as it is said (Psalms 51:5), 'and my sin is always before me,' so that he may repent from them" - to this point. Here it is explicitly said that the witnesses who warn and testify against him are the two angels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:10: And at the end of Parashat Shelach Lecha (175b), they add further: he rises to speak, the witnesses say (Psalms 34:14), "guard your tongue from evil," and so on; he stretches out his hands into worldly affairs, the witnesses say (ibid. 34:15), "turn from evil and do good." If he heeds them, well and good; if not, it is written (Zechariah 3:1), "and Satan stood at his right hand to accuse him" - they all testify against him above, concerning his sins. If a person wishes to occupy himself with the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, they all become witnesses in his defense, standing to testify good things about him at the time he needs it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:11: Further, Rashbi adds the testimony of the Torah, that it testifies against him - the reason being that it is written (Deuteronomy 31:26), "take this book of the Torah... that it may be there as a witness against you." In these words (Vayechi 227a), concerning "the world is judged in four periods" - it says there that mankind is judged in these four periods, and afterward it says: "and every single day, books are opened and deeds are written, and no one pays heed and no one inclines his ear; and the Torah testifies against him every day, and a voice cries out loudly (Proverbs 9:4), 'whoever is simple, let him turn in here; to him who lacks understanding, she says' - and no one heeds its voice. We have learned: at the time a person rises in the morning, witnesses stand opposite him and testify against him, and he pays no heed; the soul testifies before him at every moment and every hour - if he heeds, well and good, and if not, the books are open and the deeds are written" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:12: And it says further there, below: we have learned, at the time a person is judged above, his soul is brought up to the court and they judge concerning its speech, and it testifies to everything and testifies to all a person's thoughts; but it does not testify concerning deeds, for they are all written in a book - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:13: Our Sages, of blessed memory (Yalkut Mishlei, remez 959), similarly explain, in the Pesikta Rabbati, on the verse (Proverbs 20:27), "the candle of the LORD is the soul of man" - Rabbi Acha said: the soul reports every single thing a person does, in secret, in darkness or openly, and records are written before the Holy One, blessed be He, of what people do; in the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will reprove each and every one for his deeds, and they will stand astonished. A parable: of one who was married to a king's daughter, and would rise early and inquire after the king's welfare every day, and the king would say to him, you did such-and-such in your house, you became angry in such-and-such a way, you struck your servants in such-and-such a way. And when he leaves, he says to the members of his household, who told [the king] that I did this? How does he know? They said to him, fool of the world, you are married to his daughter, and you ask how he knows? His daughter reports to him! So too the soul - "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life" (Genesis 2:7) - and it reports to Him everything the person does - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:14: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (142b) that the Shechinah testifies concerning deeds done in secret, in these words: "and there are sins that are done in secret, which the angels who accompany the soul, of whom it is said (Psalms 91:11), 'for He shall command His angels concerning you,' cannot testify to - behold, the Shechinah testifies against them, this is [the meaning of] (Jeremiah 23:24), 'can a man hide himself in secret places' - because the Shechinah is upon his head, of whom it is said (Avot [Mishnah] 2:1), 'know what is above you: an eye that sees, and an ear that hears, and all your deeds are written in a book'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:15: Besides the Shechinah testifying concerning deeds done in secret, she also testifies concerning all deeds, even those done openly - and this follows the covenant that Joshua made with the children of Israel at Shechem, as it is said there (Joshua 24:26), "and he took a great stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD," and it is said (ibid. 24:27), "and Joshua said to all the people, behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the LORD which He spoke to us; it shall therefore be a witness against you, lest you deny your God." According to the plain sense, this verse makes no sense - rather, the matter is that this stone alludes to the "tested stone, the precious cornerstone" (Isaiah 28:16), "the Rock of Israel," who is the Shechinah, and therefore "it heard" and "it is a witness," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:16: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, further explains (Vayechi 222b): we have learned, Rabbi Shimon opened and said (Deuteronomy 29:28), "the hidden things belong to the LORD our God," and so on - "the hidden things" - come and see how much a person must guard himself from his sins and take heed not to transgress the will of his Master; for we have learned, everything a person does in this world, his deeds are written in a book and enter into the reckoning before the Holy King, and everything is revealed before Him - this is [the meaning of] (Jeremiah 23:24), "can a man hide himself in secret places so that I do not see him? says the LORD." If so, how should a person not be careful not to sin before his Master? And we have learned: even what a person thinks and considers in his mind, all is guarded before the Holy One, blessed be He, and is not lost from Him - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:17: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in the Sifrei, and so it is also explained in the Tikkunim, that heaven and earth are witnesses concerning a person's deeds, in these words, in the Sifrei (Yalkut, Parashat Ha'azinu, remez 868): "another interpretation: 'give ear, O heavens' - Rabbi Bena'ah used to say: when a person is found liable [to death], they do not lay a hand upon him except the witnesses first, as it is said (Deuteronomy 17:7), 'the hand of the witnesses shall be first against him, to put him to death,' and afterward the people draw near, and the hand of all the people is last. So too, when Israel does not do the will of the Omnipresent, what is said of them (ibid. 11:17)? 'And He will restrain the heavens' - and afterward punishment draws near and comes, as it is said, 'and you shall perish quickly.' And when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent, what is said of them (Hosea 2:23)? 'And it shall come to pass in that day, says the LORD, I will answer the heavens, and they shall answer the earth, and the earth shall answer the grain, and I will sow her for Myself in the land'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:18: And in the Tikkunim it says: and as it is said, there is testimony in the lower world - this is [the meaning of] (Lamentations 2:13), "what shall I testify for you, what shall I liken to you?" There is testimony in heaven and earth - this is [the meaning of] (Deuteronomy 30:19), "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:19: And so in Ra'aya Meheimna (Shoftim 275a), further: the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah are witnesses against a person - this is [the meaning of] "I call heaven and earth to witness against you today" - "heaven," this is the One of whom it is said (I Kings 8:30), "and You shall hear in heaven"; "and earth," this is the one of whom it is said (Isaiah 66:1), "and the earth is My footstool." Further, two [more] witnesses: the middle pillar [Tiferet] and the righteous one [Yesod], and these are "ed" from "Shema" - one; "ed" from "Baruch shem kevod malchuto le'olam va'ed" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:20: One must also fear the judgment stretched over him every day and every hour, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Rosh Hashanah 16a), on the verse (Job 7:18), "and You visit him every morning, and try him every moment" - it is taught: Rabbi Yosi says, a person is judged every day, as it is said, "and You visit him every morning"; Rabbi Natan says, every hour, as it is said, "try him every moment"; Rav Chisda said, from here (I Kings 8:59), "to do justice for His servant, and justice for His people Israel, as each day requires" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:21: Further, it is said in tractate Shabbat, second chapter (32a): our Rabbis taught: one who falls ill and is near death is told, confess - for so it is with all who are executed, they confess. When a person goes out into the marketplace, he should regard himself as though he had been handed over to an officer [for arrest]; if his head aches, he should regard himself as though he had been placed in stocks; if he takes to his bed and falls [ill], he should regard himself as though he had been brought up to the scaffold to be judged - and if he has great advocates, he is saved, and if not, he is not saved. These are a person's great advocates: repentance and good deeds - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:22: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Midrash Tehillim 17), on the verse (Psalms 17:8), "keep me as the pupil of the eye" - Rabbi Elazar said, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: My lamp is in your hand, and your lamp is in My hand. My lamp is in your hand - (Proverbs 6:23), "for the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light"; your lamp is in My hand - (ibid. 20:27), "the candle of the LORD is the soul of man." If you guard what is Mine, I will guard what is yours - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:23: And in the Zohar, Parashat Tzav (30b), in these words: "Rabbi Chizkiyah opened [with the verse] (Psalms 145:17), 'the LORD is righteous in all His ways, and gracious in all His works' - 'the LORD is righteous in all His ways' - we have learned, how much people must gaze upon the glory of their Master, and not stray from their way outward! For every single day judgment hangs over the world, since the world was created and stands upon judgment. And therefore a person must guard himself from his sins, for he does not know the time judgment rests upon him - he sits in his house, judgment rests upon him; he goes out of his house, judgment rests upon him, and he does not know whether he will return to his house or not; he goes out on the road, how much more so! For then judgment goes forth before him, as it is said (ibid. 85:14), 'righteousness shall go before Him.' Therefore a person must hasten with mercy before the King, to be saved from the judgment that rests in the world at the time it rests - for every single day judgment rests in the world, as it is said (ibid. 7:12), 'and God is indignant every day'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:24: And further (Korach 177a): Rabbi Chiya opened [with the verse] (Proverbs 16:14), "the king's wrath is like messengers of death, but a wise man will appease it" - how much must people guard themselves from their sins and watch their deeds! For every single day their deeds ascend on a scale and are examined above, and are written before Him; and therefore a person must be careful of his sins, for how many times is the world judged! - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:25: One must also fear that with the measure a person measures, so he is measured: if he overcomes his inclination, he causes the side of kindness to prevail over the side of judgment, and then it goes well for him; but if, Heaven forfend, he does the opposite, he causes the side of judgment to prevail over him, and then sufferings come upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:26: Similarly, it is explained in the Tikkunim (93b), in these words: "and why is Metatron called 'matteh' [staff]? Because sometimes it inclines [matteh] toward merit for the righteous, and sometimes it inclines toward guilt for the wicked; and therefore it turns from a staff into a serpent for the wicked, to strike them with it, and from a serpent into a staff for the righteous, to give them reward through it - for this angel is to the Holy One, blessed be He, like the soul that rides upon the body. And of the righteous one in this place it is said (II Samuel 23:3), 'the righteous ruler, the fear of God' - because he turns judgment into mercy. And in this matter, a change of deed is needed, for it turns from judgment to mercy - a change of name, and a change of place. But the Holy One, blessed be He, who is within, of Him it is said (Malachi 3:6), 'I, the LORD, do not change' - for He is merciful and gracious, with no judgment at all within Him, and no changes. And when a person rules over his inclination, the serpent turns into a staff, but if his inclination rules over him, the staff turns into a serpent" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:27: Further, the matter of "with the measure a person measures, so he is measured" may mean that according to how judgment was aroused above, that very same measure is bestowed upon the external forces to exact payment from him - and this is (Job 34:11), "for the work of a man He will render to him," which Rashbi explains (Korach 177a), in these words: "'for the work of a man He will render to him' - behold, a person goes about in this world and does his deeds and sins before his Master; that deed is suspended over him to render judgment to him - this is 'for the work of a man He will render to him,' that very deed will be rendered to him. Nevertheless, if he takes it to heart - once a person sets his heart and his will to return before his Master, 'his spirit and his soul shall be gathered to Him' [combining Job 34:14], into the bond of life, and he will not abandon his soul outside, to be judged with another judgment."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:28: And this is also explained in the Tikkunim (12a), concerning (Jeremiah 5:22), "who have placed the sand as a bound for the sea" - in these words: "and 'sea' refers only to the Torah; whoever transgresses it is as though he returns the world to chaos and void. And Shabbat is equal to the whole Torah - whoever transgresses it is as though he returns the world to chaos and void; and therefore the verse [Bereishit] is placed next to it [Yirah, Shabbat] - [an acronym alluding to] 'Bereishit, Yirah, Shabbat' - (Genesis 1:2), 'and the earth was chaos and void' - for it [the Torah/Shabbat] is the sand for the sea, like the collar-chain for a dog; whoever removes it from its chain causes for himself many bites of suffering that bite him. And concerning this David said (Psalms 22:21), 'deliver my soul from the sword, my only one from the power of the dog' - this is Samael, who is held in a collar," and so on - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:29: With this we may understand the punishment for transgressing any negative commandment in the Torah: for the negative commandments are fences and safeguards to hold Samael in a collar and not release him, and one who transgresses releases the rope - and therefore he causes evil for himself, to be bitten by sufferings in this world, or in the World to Come if he was not chastised in this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:30: And so it is further said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 11), on the verse (I Samuel 6:19), "and He struck the men of Beit Shemesh" - in these words: "in everything, the Holy One, blessed be He, repays measure for measure. Because the sons of Eli were corrupt in their deeds, [Israel] went out to war and four thousand of Israel were killed. Israel said, why has the LORD struck us? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: when they were angering Me in the courtyard of Israel and the courtyard of the women, you did not say this! They sent and brought the Ark of the Covenant and sounded a great blast that had no substance to it - concerning that moment it is said (Jeremiah 12:8), 'she has lifted up her voice against Me, therefore I have hated her'; immediately thirty thousand were killed and the Ark of the Covenant was captured.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:31: And even among the Philistines there was a great plague, as it is said (I Samuel 6:2), "and the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners" - and even though the priests were idol-worshippers, they had some measure of proper conduct, for they said, do not send it away empty. And when it returned and came near Beit Shemesh, and they were about two thousand cubits from Beit Shemesh, they said, let us remove the trappings and place them in a modest place, and let us see what they do for their god, whom they have thus honored - and so they did, they took their trappings and placed them in a hidden place they had.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:32: And the men of Beit Shemesh, when they saw the Ark, should have removed their garments and placed them upon their faces and fallen before it for an hour, two hours, or three hours, until the Ark of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, could be covered. But they did not do so; rather, when they saw the Ark, they laughed and stood upright and danced and spoke excessive words, as it is said (I Samuel 6:13), "and Beit Shemesh were reaping," and so on, "and they took the Ark and went their way." Therefore fifty thousand of Israel fell, and the Great Sanhedrin with them, as it is said, "and He struck the men of Beit Shemesh," and so on. And who killed all these men of Beit Shemesh? They killed themselves, for they had no proper conduct. From here they said, "with the measure a person measures," and so on. Certainly, Master of the worlds (Psalms 36:7), "Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Your judgments are a great deep" - to this point.
